To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the miRNA biogenesis pathway is tightly regulated by RNA-binding proteins; 2) miRNA biogenesis regulators are deregulated in cancer and contribute to tumorigenesis; 3) RNA-binding proteins regulate miRNA function; 4) miRNAs and their regulators can be used as biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis of cancer.
the protein class of RNA-binding proteins is involved in post-transcriptional control of microRNAs and their targets, and that these interactions are important for normal development and disease.
miRNAs are important regulators of gene expression and their expression is regulated by RNA-binding proteins, which are also important regulators of gene regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new miRNA targets, and the characterization of their biological functions in cancer.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of RNA processing, and how these processes are regulated in normal development and disease.
the molecular basis of cancer and its progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay of miRNA and RNA-binding proteins is an important mechanism in tumour development.
the interplay between RNA–RNA and RNA–protein interactions is essential for miRNA biogenesis and activity.
the miRNA–RNA-binding protein axis plays a crucial role in cancer development and progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interplay between microRNAs and RNA binding proteins is a complex and dynamic process, which can be exploited for cancer therapy.
RNA–RNA and RNA–protein interactions are essential for miRNA biogenesis and turnover and that the dysregulation of these processes may contribute to tumorigenesis.
RNA-binding proteins are important regulators of miRNAs, and that these regulatory interactions have important implications for cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA-binding proteins and miRNAs are intimately linked, and that their interactions are crucial for the regulation of gene expression.
RNA-binding proteins are important regulators of microRNAs, and that their dysregulation can lead to cancer.
miRNAs and the RNA-binding proteins that regulate them are essential for the development and progression of many cancers.
